Integrate $\frac{dy}{dx} = (4x + 1)^{1/2}$ using the reverse chain rule:
$$y = \int (4x + 1)^{1/2}\,dx = \frac{(4x + 1)^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2} \times 4} + c = \frac{(4x + 1)^{3/2}}{6} + c$$

Substitute the point $(2, 5)$ into the integrated expression to find $c$:
$$5 = \frac{(4(2) + 1)^{3/2}}{6} + c = \frac{9^{3/2}}{6} + c = \frac{27}{6} + c = \frac{9}{2} + c \implies c = 5 - \frac{9}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$$

State the equation of the curve:
$$y = \frac{(4x + 1)^{3/2}}{6} + \frac{1}{2}$$

Apply the chain rule to find $\frac{dx}{dt}$ with $\frac{dy}{dt} = 0.06\text{ units/s}$:
$$\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dt} \div \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{0.06}{3} = 0.02 \text{ units per second}$$

Differentiate $\frac{dy}{dx} = (4x + 1)^{1/2}$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:
$$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{1}{2}(4x + 1)^{-1/2} \times 4 = 2(4x + 1)^{-1/2} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{4x + 1}}$$

Multiply the second derivative by the first derivative:
$$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} \times \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{4x + 1}} \times \sqrt{4x + 1} = 2$$
$$\text{Since this product is equal to } 2 \text{ for all } x, \text{ it is constant}$$
